inlines.v: LU'CRE, noun lu'ker. [Latin lucrum.] Gain in money or goods; profit; usually in an ill sense, or with the sense of something base or unworthy. The lust of lucre and the dread of death. A bishop must be blameless - not given to filthy lucre Titus 1:7.
